A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MDP3 research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated implementation details and renumbered case studies.

before.justification: v1 reports original MDP3 benchmark experiments with VILA, MiniCPM, and LLaVA-OneVision, alongside component ablations, frame-count analyses, and inference latency measurements.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments and retains the earlier empirical results. It also adds Ovis2 evaluations, hyperparameter sensitivity tests, expanded ablations, and parallel inference timing results.

M1.justification: The conditional multi-kernel similarity, DPP selection, Markov formulation, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. MDP3-P experimentally evaluates parallel computation already described in v1; it does not introduce a new selection procedure. SigLIP text splitting and pooling are relocated explanations.

E1.justification: Both versions use Video-MME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench for video question answering, retaining the subtitle conditions and duration groups. The additions vary backbones, frame budgets, and analysis coverage within these datasets rather than introducing new datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: v2 expands comparisons in several settings: Table 1 adds Ovis2 with and without MDP3 and evaluates FRAME-VOYAGER with LLaVA-OneVision, whereas v1 reports FRAME-VOYAGER only with VILA. Table 3 adds SEVILA, and the latency comparison newly includes standard DPP. These substantially broaden the evaluated comparison set.

E3.justification: The principal 128-candidate, eight-selected-frame protocol remains. Added protocols include Ovis2 evaluation, VILA sensitivity sweeps over lambda=0.0125–12.8 and segment sizes 8–128, expanded model-by-benchmark ablations, and additional frame-budget tests. v2 also evaluates parallel computation and reports latency totals excluding common preprocessing stages previously included in v1, so those totals are not directly comparable.

E4.justification: v2 adds hyperparameter sensitivity analyses in B.4, a substantially broader component-ablation matrix in Table 5, and duration-specific frame-budget analyses for VILA and LLaVA-OneVision in Figures 7–8. It also compares serial and parallel selection latency. The six qualitative cases from v1 are retained rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions report point accuracies and average latencies without specifying repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added experiments do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results while preserving the existing Table 1 scores. New Ovis2+MDP3 scores include 63.9 on Video-MME without subtitles, 73.9 on MLVU, and 62.7 on LongVideoBench. Table 5 adds ablation outcomes, including VILA's MGK variant scoring 53.5 versus full MDP3's 50.8 on LongVideoBench. New plots report sensitivity, frame-budget failures, and 1.30-second parallel selection latency.

T1.justification: The mathematical development and Appendix A's definitions, theorem, and proofs remain unchanged. However, v2 B.8 newly asserts an O((1/k)^k) decay bound for marginal gains and attributes it to Eq. (35). This additional mathematical inference was absent in v1 and is not established by that equation.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain a training-free, model-agnostic selector combining query relevance, list-wise diversity, and sequentiality, with the same approximation and complexity claims. Explicit test-time wording and additional backbone results support existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of hyperparameter robustness and parallel overhead, explicitly acknowledges that eight frames need not be optimal, and expands discussion of failures beyond training frame budgets. Future work shifts toward test-time scaling and self-distillation. Appendix C's limitations are retained. Some new interpretations overstate the evidence, notably B.7's claim of best ablation performance across every configuration.

D1.justification: v2 adds an author code-repository link in Section 4 and specifies 32 frames for the official LLaVA-OneVision reference in Table 1. Existing SigLIP processing, kernel settings, default hyperparameters, cross-validation description, and hardware information remain; moving implementation details into B.3 does not constitute new disclosure.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hu et al.'s frame-selection work, Tang et al.'s adaptive keyframe sampling, and the Ovis2 source, while retaining the existing DPP and sequential-DPP positioning. SEVILA becomes an evaluated comparator, but its underlying paper was already cited in v1; its additional bibliography entry is not a new distinct work.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained. v2 relocates implementation material to B.3, introduces appendix subsections, renames Case Study to Qualitative Analysis, and moves the limitations before the case figures. It also edits captions, affiliation/contact text, future-work wording, and adds acknowledgments.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual evidence with two sensitivity plots, two multi-panel frame-budget figures, and Table 5's ablation matrix. Tables 1 and 3 gain rows, and the latency plot is redesigned with additional comparators and fewer displayed stages. The six unchanged case figures move from Figures 5–10 to Figures 9–14.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's limited ablation coverage and serial-only timing evaluation, v2 provides useful evidence about parameter sensitivity, component behavior across settings, and parallel overhead, plus a code-access link. These improve practical assessability. The gain is limited by new reporting errors: B.7 claims universal superiority despite Table 5's 53.5-versus-50.8 counterexample, B.4 understates Figure 4's accuracy range, and B.8 introduces an unsupported decay bound. The core method and proofs remain unchanged.
